blocked.name: The Old Gum Tree (Proclamation Tree), Glenelg North

location.address: Old Gum Tree Reserve, Glenelg North, South Australia

blocked.reason: Dead. Confirmed by two independent sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Old_Gum_Tree states the original red gum (Eucalyptus camaldulensis) 'had died by 1907' and its decayed outer surface was 'encased in concrete in 1963' to hold its shape; ABC News (2017-12-28, abc.net.au/news/2017-12-28/why-is-a-concrete-filled-bent-old-gum-tree-significant-in-sa/9289356) independently describes it as 'a bent, dead tree which is now preserved under a large canopy and filled with concrete', 'long dead but preserved as a reminder of 19th century white settlement'. No living replacement tree is mentioned at the site by either source. This is a dead husk/relic under a protective canopy, the same category as Vienna's Stock im Eisen: historically significant (site of the 1836 proclamation of the Colony of South Australia) but never a collectible living-tree entry per the project's 'we doen niet aan dode bomen' rule. Could return as context inside another Adelaide tree's story, or as a non-tree historic-site page type if that ever exists, but not as a tree entry.
